h1: Survodutide (BI 456906): what the phase 3 trials found, how it compares with tirzepatide and retatrutide, and what 'survodutide peptide' vials are
dek: A glucagon-plus-GLP-1 dual agonist with completed phase 3 trials in obesity and metabolic liver disease and no approval yet. This page tables the trials with dose, duration and result, sets it beside the approved GLP-1 drugs and its phase 3 rivals without pretending the comparisons are head-to-head, and says what a vial sold as 'survodutide peptide' actually is.

queries.heading: What is survodutide?
queries.answer: Survodutide (BI 456906) is a once-weekly injectable peptide that activates both the glucagon receptor and the GLP-1 receptor. Zealand Pharma designed it and Boehringer Ingelheim is developing it for obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic liver disease. In the phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 trial published in June 2026, adults with obesity lost 12 to 13 percent of body weight over 76 weeks against 5 percent on placebo. It is not yet approved anywhere.

queries.heading: What is the half-life of survodutide?
queries.answer: Long enough for once-weekly injection: the molecule carries a C18 fatty acid chain, the same half-life-extending device as semaglutide, so that it binds albumin and clears over about a week. The abstracts in the ledger state the design principle and the weekly schedule rather than a figure in hours.

queries.heading: Is survodutide available now?
queries.answer: Not as a medicine. As of the sources available on 2026-09-24 it has completed phase 3 in obesity and metabolic liver disease and is under regulatory review or heading there; no approval is documented, and no licensed pharmacy sells it. Vials sold online as 'survodutide peptide' are unregulated products claiming to contain an investigational drug.

information_gain: The only page that tables survodutide's human trials from phase 1 to the June 2026 phase 3 papers with dose, titration, duration and primary result (SYNCHRONIZE-1: -12.2% and -13.0% vs -5.4% at 76 weeks; SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD: 84% vs 24% achieving a 30% liver-fat reduction at 6 mg), states plainly that every comparison with tirzepatide, semaglutide and retatrutide is indirect because no head-to-head trial exists, explains the glucagon half of the mechanism and why it matters for the liver and for energy expenditure, and tells the 'survodutide peptide' searcher that the product is an unregulated copy of an investigational drug whose approval is pending.
